I got this game thinking it would be better than uplink. It was not. It was a good game. But it had alot less elements than uplink. No way to upgrade your machine, alot less programs to use. the elements of hacking were alot fewer. the story was alot shorter and sucked. This game all in all was a itty bitty version of uplink with only 3 factions. No live chat and no multiplayer and no mods.  There was nothing new compared to uplink there were actually fewer elements. You also cannot rob banks or purchase anything, and you cant just go around the world hacking everything you can and you must stick with your faction storyline and cant spoof and become someone else, this game is extremely easy compared to uplink aswell, there is no live tracing and no passive or active tracing, which makes the game alot easier for you and you cover your tracks extremely easy and even so the game wont let you advance if you dont so it even holds your hand and there are no other hackers or groups to worry about and there is no faction requirements and you cant switch between whenever you want. you either go threw csec or el storyline. This game also is not more realistic by any means all that is in this game is in uplink, there is fundamentally nothing different and no "real" hacking at all, you just use the command line more as in uplink you can get programs so you dont have to use the command line. Originally this game was a 48 hour competition and the only reason it cant be considered a rip off of uplink is because using a command line was already done by many other games about hacking(including uplink) and other genres, this game itself has a mission where you are hired by uplink to hack hacknet for stealing their product , but the names have been changed in parody except introversion. 

This game was more user friendly though, alot easier and the text was bigger.

All in all it was a fun game and I am looking forward to the march update with more progs.  also promises 4 hours of gameplay (which is probably 5 minutes of game and 4 hours of waiting for porthack to finish) 

Would i recommend this , I really really enjoyed it dispite the bits story sucking and if you liked uplink and hacker-project, and want more yes. this i recommend, but i recommend you buy it when its on sale.

If you are at all interested in hacking simulation games this is by far one of the best. The fact that it is worked predominantly on a terminal using actual unix commands may seem like a barrier to entry but is infact one of the games greatest assets when you get used to it. It allows much faster hacking than a visual click based game like say uplink (not to say uplink is a bad game).

For me coming from using linux ditros for university picking up on the commands in the terminal was very easy. The tutorial works very well at explaining what the different programs do and how to use them without explaining all of them or over explaining anything. 

It still allows for the feeling of discovery that comes from finding software on a machine and trying it out. Especially given that some software can be found before it is technically needed if you keep an eye out.

As an extra bonus too some of the commands you will learn and use frequently will allow you to do basic stuff on a unix terminal in the real world as they are built in commands.

To sum up i would absolutely recommend this game to anyone interested in playing a good hacking sim especially if you have any experience on a terminal already.

Hacknet is the lone developer's pet project, and it saddens me to give it a negative rating. Honestly, though, I just didn't enjoy the game at all. It is extraordinarily repetitive, and after a while, it feels that you're doing nothing except waiting for hacking animations to finish. With only 2 exceptions, [i] every [/i] mission can be beaten by typing the same 6-7 commands in a predetermined order. After 2-3 hours of gameplay, I kept asking myself, "why is every mission the same, and why am I being forced to do it again and again?"

I did enjoy the jokes hidden in the IRC chat logs, but even then, they repeated themselves. If you read every IRC log in the game, you'd run across the same exact joke (literally) 4-5 times. It's a bit disappointing that the developer couldn't even populate the IRC logs with unique jokes. 

As an alternative criticism... the UI has some definite issues. For example, the node map gets so cluttered that it becomes completely unusable. You're constantly forced to backtrack and look at the mission statement in order to remind yourself which nodes should be broken into. It's very frustrating, and definitely killed my sense of immersion.

All in all, I can't recommend this game. I understand that others love it, but honestly, it just wasn't for me.

Had this on my wish list for a long time and finally purchased it. Firstly, this game is not for everyone. Even if you THINK you would find it fun to play a hacking game, you will become frustrated quick when you realize it takes some work to get it right. You will be given a quick introduction, some references to read (I recommend reading them) and then tested to solve problems like your own terminal being hacked. The community is helpful, but don't expect to have your hand held with "How to do it" advice. Expect only nudges to point you in the right direction. 

Thus far, the game has been intense for me and I look forward to more self induced stress lol. There is something giddy about being where your not supposed to be. Then getting out before anyone knows you where there, or running out before you get caught. I like the feel of the terminal interface and the requirement that you need to be (or willing to be) comfortable with a command prompt. I have not encountered any bugs as of yet and the game is very stable on my Win10 system. The only gripe I have is some of the documentation on the in game archive servers is hard to read do to grammar/typos. Like it was translated to English from some other language. This was fine and added to the realism when reading IRC logs and stuff but detracted from my experience when I was trying to learn a little more.

I'm only 6 hrs in, as of this writing, but I am hooked enough to know that I would recommend HackNet.
